imgDesc.text: "O Moon, benevolent mistress, whither dost thou lead us?"
And still the moonlight flows as ever.
"We are all tainted by sin... How could we ever hope to behold the moonlight in its purest form?"

According to the teachings left by the apostle of the Golden City, all matters must be governed by reason alone, untainted by sentiment, for mortal tongues cannot articulate the sacred mysteries, and frail emotion will only profane the words of the ancestors. In service of a pure and exalted ideal, for the future of the scions of the far north, [...] these actions are as justified as they are necessary.
This decree has been approved by Lovia, humble handmaiden of the Frost Moon and the [...]th Archpriestess since the fall of Hyperborea.

Decree CMLXIII: Alternative Plan for the Sacred Heir's Selection
(All of the content that follows has been erased and cannot be read.)

...
...In accordance with the teachings of the apostle of the Golden City, all matters concerning craftsmanship and secret rites must be recorded without the taint of personal sentiment, for mortal tongues cannot articulate the sacred mysteries, and frail emotion would only profane the words of our ancestors. Do not seek to understand what lies beyond mortal intellect. Simply recite the ancient prayers with a sincere heart so that the purity of the blessings may endure.
This decree was issued by Saredne, humble handmaiden of the Frost Moon and 13th Archpriestess since the fall of Hyperborea. It is not to be defied. In the name of the mistress of the Frost Moon, the ancient laws, once obscure and difficult to understand, are now set forth in clear and concise terms, lest the faithful falter or be led astray.
...
Decree III: Elysium and the Prophecy of the Sacred Heir
Let the children of Hyperborea guard their sacred bloodline from defilement, for the heir of Elysium is destined to one day arrive.
It is hereby forbidden to marry one's closest kin. That is to say, no union shall be permitted between blood relatives.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with someone from a clan that has committed blasphemy.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with someone from a clan that has taken the life of an innocent.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with someone from a clan that has broken its oath.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with someone from a clan that does not bear an antlered crown.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with someone from a clan that has committed parricide.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with any person disturbed of mind.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with the descendants of the fae.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with a person not of the faith.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with an outlander.
Marriage is a most sacred act of virtue and must be kept pure. Therefore, let no unclean act stain our bloodline.
Let no action be taken to incur the displeasure of the mistress of the Frost Moon, and let no one betray their oaths.
Whosoever enters into marriage must first obtain the permission and blessing of the Archpriestess, lest a curse befall their bloodline.
Said curse shall plague their bloodline for seven generations, and then for seven more.
Whosoever breaks this oath shall have their horns severed with a silver blade. They who have been marked thus shall be cast into the long, lightless night.
Hear now the ancient prophecy: In the fullness of time, Elysium shall come, and with it, the sovereign ordained to rule over it shall also appear.
The false sevenfold radiance of the high heavens shall fall at her feet, and the bones of the earth shall rise to follow her.
For from her shall spring union with the world, and from her shall the first great cause be rebuilt.
Let these words of wisdom find root in your heart, and neglect not the sanctity of your blessed bloodline.
...
Decree VI: Offerings to the Sampo Mill
The children of Hyperborea shall guard the sacred treasure forged by the apostle of the Golden City at all costs.
Let it be known that the relic that is the Sampo Mill is a sacred work, for its blessing yields unending gold, grain, and salt.
Only the prophesied sacred heir shall have the power to rouse the Mill, and thus bring forth an Elysium of eternal abundance for us all.
According to the revelation of our ancestors, the Mill shall be sealed within a holy sanctum to preserve it from taint and desecration until the appointed time, when the sacred heir is born at last.
All followers below the rank of priestess shall not enter the holy sanctuary wherein the Mill is sealed. Those who violate this precept shall have a curse befall their bloodline.
Said curse shall plague their bloodline for seven generations, and then for seven more.
Before sowing in spring, an offering of wheat, goat's milk, and salt must be made unto the Sampo Mill, lest famine befall you.
At least one priestess shall be designated to chant prayers to the Mill day and night, to ensure a bountiful harvest and enduring prosperity.
...
Decree X: Offering to the Arrow of Terpikeraunas
The children of Hyperborea shall revere the Arrow of Terpikeraunas without fail.
Let it be known that this relic, forged of pure light, is a bow and arrow that can pierce the manifold darkness of the frozen night.
You shall mix the sacred oils in the following manner prescribed by the rites of the ancestors:
Take up a clean silver vessel free from all dust and water, for defilement is the root of all corruption.
Take the fat of a lamb, clear and pure, and warm it over a gentle fire.
It must not be too hot, or too cool. Do not bring it to a boil.
Add sulfur, salt, sawdust, and wax in their proper order while stirring with great care.
Stir until the substances inside the vessel are of one uniform color.
The number for your counting shall be seven hours. Six you shall not count, neither count you eight,
Excepting that you should count to seven. Five and nine are right out.
Then, anoint your bow and arrows with the holy oil,
And your arrows shall snuff out the pitch-black foe, shattering them like plates of silver.

(A thick stack of papers, hidden by an unknown someone in a secret compartment inside the back cover.)
...
In accordance with the statutes laid down by [...], all matters concerning Mekhaneikos and Tekhneikos shall be recorded objectively, concisely, and untainted by personal sentiment. Thus shall we guard against the distortion of truth via subjectivity, that the knowledge we possess may be transmitted with clarity to future generations, and serve the welfare of our people to the fullest possible extent.
The contents of this document have been approved by Spargapiris of Haxathrausa. All members of the order, beginning with the executive priests, shall commit its contents to memory and observe the prescribed procedures without deviation, until the reconstruction of civilization has reached five-sevenths completion (for further details, consult Tekhneikos Manual I-330).
...
If these words have reached your eyes, let it be known that you have completed the foundational disciplines of Mekhaneikos or Tekhneikos, and are hereby elevated to the rank of executive priest. Congratulations are in order.
Regrettably, your newly acquired title is not a privilege, but a burden of duty, hardship, and silent suffering borne for this realm and the countless lives she shelters.
You are destined to offer all of your youth and your life to preserve the last embers of civilization. Yet even with your final breath, you may never behold the Frostmoon's radiant light, nor see the dawn break once more upon our beautiful homeland. For the lights of the far north have been extinguished, and countless generations are condemned to cower in darkest night. No miracle has ever graced this tainted sublunary sphere, and tears have never delivered our kin from sorrow.
Then what purpose, if any, lies in all that you shall do from this moment hence?
I suppose, then, it is for an ethereal dream. A dream of countless tomorrows, for an infinity of futures yet unborn.
Only through our blood, our tears, and our toil shall our children be granted the chance to behold the glorious era and the lost Elysium we once knew. On that day, none shall weep for suffering, nor fear hunger or cold. All beings shall love one another as brothers and sisters, and all shall dwell in joy and peace.
This shall be our final and greatest dream: That our kin shall no longer be mired in superstition and barbarism. For the hope once envisioned by gods and mortals alike, we must push forward. There is no path but through.
Sear these words into your mind before you proceed to read the assessment records and operating procedures.
Hold fast to our dream of tomorrow, and let not its light be dimmed by the dust of neglect.
— Spargapiris of Haxathrausa, Acting Archpriestess of Hyperborea
...
Protocol III: Final Evaluation on Bloodline Selection and Purification
Upon evaluation and confirmation by the Acting Archpriestess and the Senior Executive Tekhneikos Priestess, the Seed of Life Project from the Hyperborea era —henceforth referred to as the Sacred Heir Project — has been deemed to no longer be viable within the bounds of its original planned parameters. The priest who led the project, Vinda of Hithamthrausa, has passed beyond, and the essential Tekhneikos processes and Mekhaneikos apparatuses required for its continuation were lost in the fall of Hyperborea. These include, but are not limited to:
· The process of [...] cutting and modification;
· The process of [...] creation and reconstruction;
· The [...] and [...] processes, which were of the fae;
· The adaptive [...] editing process;
· ...
The aforementioned Tekhneikos processes are, at present, irreproducible.
After due deliberation, the following alternative protocol has been deemed acceptable:
· The purification of existing [...] is to be performed through controlled artificial selection, using methods primitive and inefficient.
· The phenotypic stability of each generation shall be recorded. Then, from this data, the most suitable pairs for union shall be identified, and non-coercive means employed to persuade the parties to join in union.
· Should persuasion fail to meet the criteria detailed in Tekhneikos Manual O-90, promptly proceed to the next priority match, and continue in like fashion.
· To minimize risk of disease, the Bloodline Proximity Index of all breeding pairs shall not exceed [...]. Accordingly, no individuals shall be joined in union if they share common ancestry within five generations.
This course of action is expected to yield outcomes approaching the original objective after [...] successive generations of refinement and selection. At such time, the one prophesied, the newborn Sacred Heir, shall arise. Without the need for ritual implements, nor the forfeiture of their soul, this heir shall command the pure, unaltered elemental forces at will, and shall at last attain fusion with the World.
Note: In light of projected population growth and the limits of environmental carrying capacity, it is anticipated that the practice of widespread artificial breeding may be terminated after seven generations. Thereafter, limited intermarriage with select outlanders may then be sanctioned (details in Tekhneikos Manual I-1012). Furthermore, it is hereby affirmed that, once the continuity of civilization has been assured, the descendants of the far north shall be granted the sovereign right to determine their own destinies.
...
Protocol VI: The Subatomic Assembling Mass-Energy Patterning Orb (Sealed)
The project of constructing this supremely advanced Mekhaneikos construct was personally overseen by [...] and is not fully understood at this time. It was designed to reconstruct matter at the subatomic scale, or to transmute matter directly into stable energy, which would then be released in the form of [...].
Of all the known highest-tier Mekhaneikos constructs dating to the time of Hyperborea, only the Subatomic Assembling Mass-energy Patterning Orb (hereafter referred to as the "SAMPO") has endured to the present age. Its structure remains largely intact, granting it immense symbolic significance. However, a formal evaluation by the Acting Archpriestess and the Senior Executive Mekhaneikos Priestess has determined that the device, in its current state, is no longer functional. The collaborative control module connected to the device was lost during the fall of Hyperborea and cannot be replicated with existing technologies. In the absence of this module, proper activation of the SAMPO is impossible, and it is presumed that even a forced restart would fail to correctly reconfigure said device (refer to appendix for more details).
After due deliberation, it is resolved that the device shall be sealed indefinitely, with no re-evaluation of its activation viability for a period of [...] generations. All personnel without explicit authorization from the Archpriestess may not breach the seal. This will prevent unnecessary accidental damage to the device.
Note: The Senior Executive Mekhaneikos Priestess, Ariapeithea of Massagetae, has proposed a theoretically viable bypass protocol. Namely, the controlled input of [...] Realm Energy or [...] Realm Energy (refer to Mekhaneikos Manual D-503 for the possibility of the latter) at a specific carrier frequency, which may circumvent the collaborative control module and forcibly initiate the SAMPO. Upon formal evaluation, however, the proposed method was determined to pose unacceptable safety risks, with the probability of system destabilization and ensuing [...] exceeding [...]. In light of these findings, the original decision shall stand.
...
Protocol X: The Arrow of Terpikeraunas
The subject of the project is a low-tier Mekhaneikos device of the Hyperborea era, designed to solidify [...] Realm Energy into a semi-crystalline polymeric form. Once stabilized, the material is subjected to a high-frequency [...] spiral acceleration and subsequently launched, thereby purging a designated area of [...] Realm Energy contamination.
The Acting Archpriestess and the Senior Executive Mekhaneikos Priestess have jointly affirmed that the device's remanufacture is viable. This work shall proceed under the oversight of Senior Executive Mekhaneikos Priestess Ariapeithea of Massagetae, with the prototype device projected for completion within [...] standard quarters.
Upon completion, the prototype apparatus shall be subject to regular lubrication with ointments to prevent avoidable safety incidents. (Refer to Mekhaneikos Manual D-306 for more details.)

customize.text: Frostmoon Scions

More than six thousand years ago, Three Moons shone in the sky: the Eternal Moon, the Frost Moon, and the Iridescent Moon. They were created by Teyvat's ruler, the primeval dragon Nibelung, before he set out to find salvation for his world. Nibelung raised three bright moons from the ground and bound this tiny world tightly with the chains of the tides. Moonlight would illuminate the bountiful land throughout the Long Night of the end, until the dragon returned from the mist-shrouded realm. Yet, as one thousand years passed into another, the three moon sisters awaited in vain the return of their former lord. Until one day, the winged Descender appeared, treading upon the morning star. It was not the great enemy that would extinguish the stars, nor did it seem intent on plundering the wellspring sustaining the world's existence. Faced with this uninvited guest, the three guardians who represented the will of the planet debated endlessly: the youngest sister opposed the Descender, but the elder sisters decided to see what would happen. The Heavenly Principle created angels and humans, led by the heavenly messengers. They wandered among the dark mortals, sowing prosperity and wisdom everywhere, and eventually, this prosperity ignited the flame of reason, which awakened a whisper of doubt.

Over time, the Moon Goddesses began to notice that their love differed from that of the Heavenly Principles. The Descender believed that free will invites nothing but uncertainty and calamity, and that mortals who transgressed the laws of reason must be punished, like overgrown branches on a tree must be pruned. They bore an almost paranoid hostility and fear toward the desire of certain life forms to seek power and destroyed insufficiently sacred civilizations, even if it meant sending them into oblivion. They cast down celestial nails as manifestations of their power to punish the civilizations of the world below. Their rules brought order, but the price people paid for merely testing the limits of those rules was far too great. In a single night, the golden kingdom of Hyperborea fell like a fig tree, and across the frozen northern plain, from the holy citadel to the ancient capital, dark blue crystal nails annihilated every last city with even the most minuscule sign of life. Those who survived by the grace of being nowhere near the cities at the time could only cling to life amidst the freezing wind and snow. With no refuge left to them, they simply waited for destruction to find them in the hollow dark. Their prosperity turned to dust, and the gods remained silent, unmoved by cries, curses, or reproach. Only one celestial ruler responded to the mortals' pain. This was the Goddess of the Frost Moon, Canon, queen of the celestial chariot and of light, a heavenly agent whose origin was one with that of the world. Moved by pity and a deeper, unspoken wish, Canon heeded the survivors' prayers. According to legend, she spun gleaming threads from the silver glow to lead the displaced across the frozen plains, and where her tears, full of longing, fell upon the frost-covered soil of the far north, they blossomed into lilies that would stand eternal in the icy winds. The proud descendants of Hyperborea called themselves the Frostmoon Scions, in honor of the divinity who gave humanity new life.

When Three Moons still shone in the sky, the people of the golden kingdom learned to use the lunar tides to power their magics, but were in turn affected by those same ebbs and flows, and some of them thus had horned crowns akin to deer antlers grow from their heads. In the legends of the Frostmoon Scions, the antler crown of Moonchanters today was a gift from the Frost Moon at the moment of its obliteration. The silver tree was splintered, and bereft of white branches they might find, the priesthood pleaded for new coronals, and out of pity, the mistress of the moon wove holy crowns for them out of flawless moonlight, ones innate to their birth.

customize.text: Hyperborea's Legacy

More than six thousand years ago, the first angel, the first daughter of the Heavenly Principles, transferred the power of creation from the Master of the Heavens into the hands of mortals, dreaming that these tiny beings would one day create a perfect being capable of merging with the entire world. Turning to forbidden methods, artisans forged countless Fae spirits upon the bones of giant beasts. Having spun fallen frostmoon light into flawless flesh and blood, they clad it in forms once frail and weak. Furthermore, under the guidance of the first angel and the voyager from a distant world, the Hyperboreans launched the "Elysium Project." They hoped to transform the world into an Elysium for humankind alone. After relentless experimentation, they mastered the power of tailoring and refining the Seeds of Life. The new humans born after such "adjustments" were supposed to wield elemental forces at will. They hoped that their descendants would produce enough food to free all life from hunger, unlock primordial secrets, freely transform matter into energy and vice versa, create entire worlds with their thoughts, and explore the true cosmos. But when the golden city fell, so did the dreams of the Hyperboreans. The Frostmoon Scions acquired the title of executive priest, a burden of duty, hardship, and silent suffering for the preservation of the last vestiges of civilization. They believed that by sacrificing their blood, souls, and sweat, they would grant their descendants the hope of seeing an era of splendor and a lost Elysium. No one would cry in pain anymore, and no one would suffer from the cold. Everyone would live together as brothers and sisters, everyone would be happy, and peace would reign.
The Hyperboreans left the Frostmoon Scions with several devices created with the help of the Mekhaneikos. The only supremely advanced device was the Subatomic Assembling Mass-Energy Patterning Orb, later known as the Sampo Mill. It was designed to reconstruct matter at the subatomic scale, that is, or to transmute matter directly into stable energy. Although its structure remained largely intact, the device was unusable because the collaborative control module connected to the device was lost during the fall of Hyperborea and couldn't be replicated with existing technologies. One of the priestesses proposed using a controlled input of energy from the two Realms at a specific carrier frequency to bypass the collaborative control module and forcibly initiate the SAMPO, but an assessment revealed that the proposed protocol was unsafe, as it risked destabilizing the system. Following the discussion, it was decided to seal the device indefinitely without re-evaluating its feasibility. The SAMPO gradually transformed from a device into a religious symbol. They believed that only the heir foretold in the prophecy could awaken the Mill and create an Elysium of eternal abundance for them. The Frostmoon Scions sacrificed wheat, goat's milk, and salt to the Sampo Mill to protect them from disaster, and appointed priestesses to chant hymns day and night to ensure a rich harvest and prosperity.
The Frostmoon Scions also continued the
of the Hyperborean era. Since the core processes of the Tekhneikos and the Mekhaneikos apparatus, including the process of creating Fae and editing the Seeds of Life, were lost during the fall of Hyperborea, it was decided to purify the blood of the Frostmoon Scions through controlled selection. The phenotypic stability of each generation had to be recorded, and then, from this data, the most suitable pairs for union should have been identified, and non-coercive means employed to persuade the parties to join in union. If the persuasion failed to meet the criteria, it would proceed to a prompt switch to the next priority match and continue in like fashion. The descendants of Hyperborea were forbidden to marry relatives, murderers and blasphemers, oathbreakers, people without an antlered crown, the insane, the descendants of the Fae, unbelievers, and outlanders. It was assumed that this would result in the birth of the prophesied Sacred Heir, who would freely command the pure, unaltered elemental forces at will, without resorting to ritual implements or sacrificing their soul, thereby achieving fusion with the world.

A low-tier device of the Mekhaneikos, created during the Hyperborean era and preserved to this day, is the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. This device is designed to solidify the Light Realm into a semi-crystalline polymeric form, which was then subjected to high frequencies with spiral acceleration, thereby purging a designated area of the Void Realm contamination. Unlike the Sampo Mill, the Arrow of Terpikeraunas could be restored and reused. Over time, the device also acquired religious significance, so priests prepared sacred oil and then anointed their bows and arrows with it, so that they would strike down dark enemies and shatter them into fragments like a silver disk.

customize.text: Sacred Heir

More than five hundred years ago, when the Frost Moon no longer cast its gaze on the Frostmoon Scions, and even those born of the purest blood could no longer wield its light, an outsider named Lovia was adopted by the Archpriestess. Compassionate and kind, the handmaiden firmly believed in all that was "right," and therefore, only by choosing the absolutely "right" path could all things be brought to happiness. To walk the path of righteousness is to give grain to the hungry and tend the sick through the long night, mend the wounds of suspicion with sincerity and understanding, and soothe the troubled hearts of one's kin. True kindness was ultimately meant to become a gentle flame, warming cold and indifferent hearts in the night, driving away resentment and hatred. As the hearts of the Frostmoon Scions grew ever more distant and the whispers of doubt ever louder, the decrepit Archpriestess placed her adopted daughter upon the shaky sacred throne, hoping that her kindness would pacify the disunited flock, even though the bright moonlight never flowed through her veins.

<color=#ffffffd9>"O, my kind child Lovia, the purest of them all, receive this Archpriestess's staff.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Only your mercy and compassion can open the eyes of the lost lambs and bless them with serene, gentle joy.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Only you can give them the happiness known to the weak — the comfort of being led — for they are born with hearts that ache to belong.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Only you can correct the twisted falsehoods that lurk in the shadows beneath the moon, for there is no other path but the way of truth.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>The mistress of the Frost Moon has already spun every path in the world with her silver thread, and all things now move in step with the thread's silent dance."</color>

And so Lovia firmly believed in this truth, casting a compassionate gaze upon her flock. Until her sworn younger sister, a maiden of the purest blood in all the far north, sacrificed herself, protecting Lovia from a traitor. Then, Lovia realized that the path she had chosen had not been the "right" one at all, and that her gentle kindness had been an unforgivable lie. If the true moon were to withhold its gift of hope, then let lies be spun into a gentle dawn that would stir the long-awaited fervor of the weak and grant the suffering lambs a paradise where all may rest as equals. Should the ethereal new moon never rise again, then let absolute authority reign over the mortal dream, so that the straying flock might once more be made obedient and no longer grieve for gifts bestowed in vain. The Archpriestess believed this could be the only salvation for lost souls, and anyone who dared challenge this would be washed away in blood for their crimes. And so, the merciful and kind maiden, who wept over all the sorrows and griefs of the sublunary world, forged herself an antlered crown from cold, unwavering iron and ascended the sacred throne.
According to prophecy, the daughter of Lovia's younger sister was to bear a sacred heir destined to rule Elysium. But when the girl met a young man from the northern kingdom, she felt a love she had never felt before and abandoned her mission for the sake of the young officer. For this new feeling, this foolishness called love, she cut off her antlered crown and threw it onto the snowy ground. She wanted her unborn son, Avrelian, to live in peace and joy, never to set foot on the lands of Nod-Krai or believe in dreams of "Elysium." Though she had long since left her homeland, the new life growing within her awakened long-dormant visions of the fall of civilizations and the future of her homeland. She saw how humans first enjoyed wisdom and prosperity, followed by greed and selfish desires, each masked by noble names. From them followed hatred, curses, betrayal, strife, plunder, slaughter, and kin turning against kin. Cities were scattered across the land, some following the path of good, others the path of evil, and the divine envoys remained silent and did not interfere. But when the kings of men dared to test the
the great towers fell in flame. Like all tragic illusions, that boundless Elysium would crumble. The dying world drew near its end, and only the shadows of the past remained in its halls. But Avrelian's voice, which she had never heard before, full of compassion as soft as light, always whispered to her from the dead end of darkness and pain: <color=#ffffffd9>"I shall bring an end to the warriors of this land and raise a boundless Elysium in their place. I do this not to be king, but so that no other can ever claim that role."</color>

Dreaming of creating an "Elysium," the Archpriestess Lovia allied herself with the Belyi Tsar's favorite, the mad monk, Rotwang. One day, he saw a pitch-black Elysium and desired to attain it. When Rotwang sent spies to capture the blessed maiden and return her to the homeland she was destined to love, the girl saw her lover's blood spilling beneath her feet and slit her throat. Lovia then turned to a lesser branch of the bloodline for spares, but the twin sisters, Aila and Alia, born into this family, were pale shadows of the maiden they were destined to replace. This meant that hundreds of years might pass before a child of sufficient purity would be born, and Lovia was not prepared to wait. To purify the sisters' blood, she began feeding them the blood of the Frostmoon Scions. The Archpriestess was unaware that the blessed maiden had given birth to a son, Avrelian, who, according to prophecy, would lead to Elysium. After the loss of his parents, Avrelian was adopted by a private officer named Mikhnenko, and thanks to this, the boy was able to enroll in the Snezhnayan Royal Military Academy. But shortly after Avrelian was promoted to officer, he was marked as "died in the line of duty," a plot hatched by Rotwang and the Duke of the Pale Star court. Avrelian later returned to Nod-Krai and became the great thief Reed Miller.

Sisters Aila and Alia were born imperfect, sharing a single breath. In the brief moments between agonies, moments that should have been filled with joy, they huddled together, drawing what little warmth they could from each other. They had never seen their parents, nor had they ever heard the wind whispering through the groves. The two of them had only their grandmother, and the only way they'd seen the world was through the pages of a faded storybook. The worn pages revealed a world they had never seen: a single white bird, a streak of grace, gliding beneath a perfect moon. As they admired the free creatures of the fairy tales, the two children made a promise to each other that one day, the two of them would fly together like the white birds in the vast sky. "Since the day we were born, it's always been just the two of us. When the day comes for us to leave, let's live the rest of our lives together." But Aila's older sister, Alia, did not keep her promise and set off alone on a long journey that turned out not to be a flight toward a brighter future, but a fall into a much darker night. When the blessed lady's child, Avrelian, returned to Nod-Krai, not becoming the chosen heir of the Frostmoon Scions, Alia fled with him, leaving Aila alone. From then on, all hope for the birth of the sacred heir fell on the younger sister, and she grew up under the control of the Archpriestess, never forgiving Avrelian. For the Frostmoon Scions, Alia became a traitor whose name was erased from history. With unwavering faithfulness, Aila carried out every last one of the venerable Archpriestess's commands, no matter how dreadful the punishments cloaked by her soft words. Whether someone's thread was to be severed by a sharp silver blade, or another's singing voice must be silenced in the dead of night, all sins were borne to purify the holy blood bestowed by the moon, for only by drinking crimson water could one hone absolute flawlessness.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Here, drink this pure moonlight, my beloved child, my most cherished child!"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Let it weave into your flesh and blood, so that you too may be worthy of the gods' grace."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Look to the apostle of the Golden City. How he drank bitter wine and fought for the freedom of his compatriots!"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Like him, you must embrace this joyous pain, for from it, perfection will one day be born."</color>

To achieve his goals, Professor Rotwang convinced Avrelian to obtain the Sampo Mill from the Frostmoon Scions, promising him to create an Elysium together, and that's when Alia met him. Back then, the entirety of Hiisi Island was encircled by a golden wall even taller than Mont Esus in Fontaine, and no outlander could get in there. Later, he was convinced by a noble friend to walk away from the Treasure Hoarders, leave everything behind, and go to Snezhnograd to explain himself to the Belyi Tsar. However, he was promptly sent to his death without so much as a glimpse of the Tsar. After Avrelian's death, a man named Solovei arrived in Nod-Krai and began to interfere with Lovia and Rotwang's plans. When he met Aila, the Archpriestess wanted to convince the girl to use her wisdom to lure him to the sanctuary and pierce his heart with a sword from behind to sever the thread of his evil. The only answer the Archpriestess received was silence, which she took for agreement. The girl's long-term obedience made her sincerely believe that suffering never caused her to feel resentful. And when Aila realized that the Archpriestess had deceived her and pierced her with a blade made of pure silver, Lovia could not understand the reason for this betrayal.
<color=#ffffffd9>"Heh... Mr. Solovei was right. You were just lying to us, Grandma Lovia."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"If that were not the case... why would you bleed dawn-light crimson, rather than moonlit silver, when your thread was cut?"</color>

Aila's older sister, Alia, understood that using the Sampo Mill could pose a grave danger to all of Nod-Krai, so she pretended to be Solovei's close friend to gain his trust. When Professor Rotwang built a heaven-reaching tower in Nod-Krai, named the Pillar of Embla, he intended to use the Sampo Mill to siphon the land's power and, through that tower, ascend to the "Elysium" he believed lay beyond the sky. If his scheme succeeded, all of Nod-Krai — its soil and every living being upon it — would have become fuel for his ascent. Alia and Solovei did all they could to stop him, but at the time, they were too weak. When they reached the Pillar of Embla, Rotwang was one step away from his goal. Realizing there was no other choice, Alia cast herself into the Sampo Mill and, with her own body, ignited it with the purified blood of the Frostmoon Scions. Alia was drawn into the Mill, and by chance, she briefly lingered in the crack between time and space. Alia's sacrifice thwarted the Professor's plans and destroyed him for the first time.

customize.text: Moonchanter

Due to the purification of her blood, Aila foresaw that decades later, a new moon goddess would be born, and everything Lovia had so long and desperately sought would be in vain. She didn't know if she would live to see that day, as she couldn't see her own threads of fate, but she prayed that it wouldn't happen, for sinners are unworthy of seeing the pure light of the moon. But to prepare the Frostmoon Scions, she had to convince people that the new moon would delight only in kindness, friendship, and mutual aid. Otherwise, no matter how noble the ideal, it will only wither and fade into the filth that lies beneath the moon. The new moon goddess was not obligated to give anything in return to her followers and was not obligated to be the ideal deity for everyone. Thus, Aila became the first Moonchanter, rewrote the old prayers, hymns, and doctrines of the Frostmoon Scions, and consigned the name of Lovia to oblivion. The chamber where the Archpriestess's works were preserved was sealed, lest future descendants of the Frostmoon Scions bear the burden of her sins. And although Aila considered herself a sinner, unworthy of witnessing the birth of a new moon goddess, she witnessed her birth and personally carved a statue on Hiisi Island.

When
struck Teyvat five hundred years ago, the court of the Belyi Tsar could no longer mind the remote borderlands beyond the snowy plains. The horde of pitch-black beasts tore across the barren land, destroying all traces of past civilization. Countless souls lie buried within the ancient ruins, innumerable heroes faded where mists now stray. It was not until Silvestr arrived at the abandoned by the gods Nod-Krai. To combat the forces of the Abyss and the Wild Hunt, Aila, the Moonchanter, shared with Solovei, whom she saw as a hero destined to protect Elysium, the sacred relic of the Frostmoon Scions, the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. Borrowing the priestess's power, Solovei raised that first beam of light and, in the name of the moon, banished the darkness to those lightless ruins, burying it deep down alongside the nightmare-torn souls. Since Aila had the ability to see the future, she foresaw Rotwang's return from the impenetrable darkness, and Solovei decided to found an order that would meet the threat with Hyperborean technology. He named this order the Lightkeepers, in honor of the flame Aila had ignited, and he himself became the first Torchforger and the first Starshyna. <color=#ffffffd9>"Twice shall that undying serpent rise again, but thrice shall he be struck down... And at last shall he be laid to rest by the heroes of the sublunary sphere..."</color> After Rotwang's first "death" at the Pillar of Embla, he returned as a being woven from the Abyss. Solovei and Aila were able to push the demon and his followers back to Kipumaki Cliff and seal him there. Since Aila knew that the seal placed on Rotwang would one day weaken and he would return to the world for a third time, she recorded her image to leave a message for the hero of the sublunary world who would rid the world of the undying serpent. Five hundred years after Rotwang's second death, the Traveler arrived in Nod-Krai, whom the priestess recognized as the protector of Elysium. Aila guided them and the priestess of the Frostmoon Scions, using the Ancient Moon Remnants, whose fall she had also foreseen, to remove the seal from the Court of the First Edict. She left them the last sword, forged in moonlight by the Apostle of the Far North. It was with this blade that Aila once slew the Archpriestess Lovia, and with it she offered the first drop of silver blood to the newborn moon goddess.

When the new Moon Goddess was born, the Frostmoon Scions had nothing but hope. Before she could comprehend what was happening, they named her their goddess, Kuutar, and she had no reason to refuse. Like an infant accidentally swapped, she embraced their faith, and they, in turn, embraced her. But despite the efforts of the first Moonchanter, the Frostmoon Scions cared more about their own beliefs than about the truth. The feeling that something was wrong only fueled their greed and doubt. They constantly asked for weapons to be forged, enemies to be driven away, lands to be expanded, wounds to be healed, and strength to be granted. They prayed to Kuutar for everything, and she fulfilled their will until she could no longer answer, her strength draining. The goddess knew that the moon in the sky was not real, and her true home lay beyond the heavens. Teyvat continually rejected her, causing her to lose strength. Since Kuutar felt no home among the Frostmoon Scions, she abandoned them. Only many years later did she return to Hiisi Island and, thanks to the new Moonchanter, Lauma, decided to become part of their family.

By the time of Lauma's birth, the pure blood of the descendants of Hyperborea had practically vanished, and the appearance of silver blood and horns had become a great rarity. And when Lauma was born, her horns growing in the moonlight, her silver blood resembling the moon reflected in water, she became a source of hope for the Frostmoon Scions and proof that the Moon Goddess had not abandoned them. From the moment she was born, Lauma was appointed the new Moonchanter and given the Moon Wheel. At the edge of the world, among the Frostmoon Scions forgotten by time, Lauma became a beacon of hope in difficult times, like a fire lit in a blizzard. Because of the purity of her blood, Lauma had a special sensitivity to kuuvahki that only those born once a century are born with. She felt that the full moon in the sky, though shining, was lifeless and empty. And the true tides that stirred her soul and made her antler crown grow were somewhere far beyond her reach. And although this feeling troubled her, she chose to live in "concealment," not wanting to shake the faith of the Frostmoon Scions. One day, after the Ancient Moon Remnants fell to earth, she encountered Kuutar, who had by then returned to Hiisi Island. Lauma asked the Moon Goddess why she had left the Frostmoon Scions and realized they had betrayed her: for many years, they had walked a path of error, praying to a false moon and a goddess who could no longer answer them. After this, the Moonchanter decided to tell the Frostmoon Scions the truth about the false sky and the true Frost Moon. Some were unable to accept the truth and left the society forever, but others remained, ready to change together.

customize.text: Traditions

is a traditional festival celebrated by the Frostmoon Scions in honor of the birth of the Moon Goddess, Kuutar. Initially a purely religious holiday, it eventually evolved into the most popular festival in Nod-Krai, celebrated even by ordinary residents. When the Frostmoon Scions learned that their beliefs were false, the Moon-Prayer Night became more of a local custom than a celebration of the Moon Goddess. The holiday has no fixed date and depends on the movement of the Moon, as the Moon is closest to Teyvat on the Moon-Prayer Night. The Frostmoon Scions make a rough estimate and then determine the exact time by observing changes in the Verdant Crests and Moon-Prayer Blossoms. On this day, the crescent moon at the top branches of the Verdant Crest turns into a full moon, and the Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with a special radiance, considered a blessed omen. The Verdant Crest is a Divine Tree that appeared at the birth of the Moon Maiden five centuries ago, and is therefore considered a symbol of Kuutar. The Verdant Crests are mentioned in the ancient rituals of the Frostmoon Scions in prayers to the Ruler of Time, Istaroth, although they could not have existed at that time.

One day, a special fragment of the Ancient Moon's Remnants called the Moon Marrow, possessing the power of the Goddess of the Eternal Moon, Aria, fell on Hiisi Island. This special relic allowed the true past to be revealed at the moment when kuuvahki in Nod-Krai reaches its peak, on the Moon-Prayer Night. Only the Moonchanter has the right to take the Moon Marrow from its sealed sanctuary once a year. Thanks to the Moon Marrow, the Traveler was able to see their spaceship arrive in Nod-Krai long ago. Although no one had left the ship during this time, during the Cataclysm, the Traveler's twin came from outside to free them. When the Frostmoon Scions' blood was still strong, under special circumstances, the Moonchanter could act as a vessel and hold the relic within their body, but the longest they could hold it was two days. Only the Traveler can effortlessly hold the Moon Marrow within themselves, enhancing their perception of kuuvahki.

The Frostmoon Scions have always advocated coexistence with nature, encouraging their followers to build positive relationships with the beasts of the wild. At the same time, to ensure their animal friends build the strength to withstand hardship and disasters, they put selected animals with whom they share a special bond through a unique sort of training. This is how the "Spirit Envoy Championship" was born, a trial designed to find the strongest human-animal pair by means of friendly sparring. In previous years, the competition was restricted to the Frostmoon Scions only, but in the last year, participants from all over the world were invited to participate.
